stanzas.sanskrit:
उत्तानपादनृपतेर्मनुनन्दनस्य
जाया बभूव सुरुचिर्नितरामभीष्टा ।
अन्या सुनीतिरिति भर्तुरनादृता सा
त्वामेव नित्यमगतिः शरणं गताऽभूत् ॥ १७-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Swayambhu Manu's Son Uttanapada had two wives, Suneethi and Suruchi.
Suruchi was extremely dear to the King Uttanapada that he neglected his other wife Suneethi.
Because of this grief, Suneethi surrendered at the feet of Lord.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
uttānapādanṛpatermanunandanasya
jāyā babhūva surucirnitarāmabhīṣṭā |
anyā sunītiriti bharturanādṛtā sā
tvāmeva nityamagatiḥ śaraṇaṃ gatā’bhūt || 17-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अङ्के पितुः सुरुचिपुत्रकमुत्तमं तं
दृष्ट्वा ध्रुवः किल सुनीतिसुतोऽधिरोक्ष्यन् ।
आचिक्षिपे किल शिशुः सुतरां सुरुच्या
दुःसन्त्यजा खलु भवद्विमुखैरसूया ॥ १७-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: One day Dhruva, Suneethi's five year old son wished to sit on his father's lap after seeing his step brother Uttama seated. Suruchi scolded Dhruva harshly and pushed him away due to her jealousy which arises out of her lack of devotion for Lord.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
aṅke pituḥ suruciputrakamuttamaṃ taṃ
dṛṣṭvā dhruvaḥ kila sunītisuto’dhirokṣyan |
ācikṣipe kila śiśuḥ sutarāṃ surucyā
duḥsantyajā khalu bhavadvimukhairasūyā || 17-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वन्मोहिते पितरि पश्यति दारवश्ये
दूरं दुरुक्तिनिहतः स गतो निजाम्बाम् ।
साऽपि स्वकर्मगतिसन्तरणाय पुंसां
त्वत्पादमेव शरणं शिशवे शशंस ॥ १७-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Suneethi consoled her son and advised Dhruva that the one way to overcome the evil effects of one’s own past karma was to take shelter at Lord’s feet.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvanmohite pitari paśyati dāravaśye
dūraṃ duruktinihataḥ sa gato nijāmbām |
sā’pi svakarmagatisantaraṇāya puṃsāṃ
tvatpādameva śaraṇaṃ śiśave śaśaṃsa || 17-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
आकर्ण्य सोऽपि भवदर्चननिश्चितात्मा
मानी निरेत्य नगरात् किल पञ्चवर्षः ।
सन्दृष्टनारदनिवेदितमन्त्रमार्ग-
-स्त्वामारराध तपसा मधुकाननान्ते ॥ १७-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Dhruva left to forest and met Sage Narada on his way. Sage Narada gave Dwadashakshara Mantram and taught him how to perform devotion & how the Lord will look like. He reached Madhuvanam and performed penance for 5 months.

Mantram :
*OM NAMO BHAGAVATHE VAASUDEVAAYA*
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ākarṇya so’pi bhavadarcananiścitātmā
mānī niretya nagarāt kila pañcavarṣaḥ |
sandṛṣṭanāradaniveditamantramārga-
-stvāmārarādha tapasā madhukānanānte || 17-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
ताते विषण्णहृदये नगरीं गतेन
श्रीनारदेन परिसान्त्वितचित्तवृत्तौ ।
बालस्त्वदर्पितमनाः क्रमवर्धितेन
निन्ये कठोरतपसा किल पञ्चमासान् ॥ १७-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Father Uttanapada was very worried that he was the reason for Dhruva to leave for penance at such a young age. Sage Naradha consoled the Father on reaching to his kingdom. Dhruva was totally devoted for 5 months in penance seeking the feet of Lord.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tāte viṣaṇṇahṛdaye nagarīṃ gatena
śrīnāradena parisāntvitacittavṛttau |
bālastvadarpitamanāḥ kramavardhitena
ninye kaṭhoratapasā kila pañcamāsān || 17-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तावत् तपोबलनिरुच्छ्वसिते दिगन्ते
देवार्थितस्त्वमुदयत्करुणार्द्रचेताः ।
त्वद्रूपचिद्रसनिलीनमतेः पुरस्ता-
-दाविर्बभूविथ विभो गरुडाधिरूढः ॥ १७-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
On the fifth month, Dhruva controlled his breath perfectly and standing on only one leg meditated on the Parabrahman. Dhruva captured the Supreme God within his heart. Due to his controlled breath and becoming practically one in heaviness with Lord Vishnu, the universal breathing became choked. The demigods felt suffocated and took shelter of the Supreme Lord.
The Lord himself went to Madhuvanam and gave darshan to Dhruva appearing as seated on Garuda.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tāvat tapobalanirucchvasite digante
devārthitastvamudayatkaruṇārdracetāḥ |
tvadrūpacidrasanilīnamateḥ purastā-
-dāvirbabhūvitha vibho garuḍādhirūḍhaḥ || 17-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वद्दर्शनप्रमदभारतरङ्गितं तं
दृग्भ्यां निमग्नमिव रूपरसायने ते ।
तुष्टूषमाणमवगम्य कपोलदेशे
संस्पृष्टवानसि दरेण तथाऽऽदरेण ॥ १७-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Soaked in bliss, Dhuruva was speechless, Lord touched the cheek of the boy with his conchshell (பாஞ்சஜன்யம்). Dhuruva sang the glory of the God, enlightened with the knowledge gained from the Lord.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvaddarśanapramadabhārataraṅgitaṃ taṃ
dṛgbhyāṃ nimagnamiva rūparasāyane te |
tuṣṭūṣamāṇamavagamya kapoladeśe
saṃspṛṣṭavānasi dareṇa tathā”dareṇa || 17-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तावद्विबोधविमलं प्रणुवन्तमेन-
-माभाषथास्त्वमवगम्य तदीयभावम् ।
राज्यं चिरं समनुभूय भजस्व भूयः
सर्वोत्तरं ध्रुवपदं विनिवृत्तिहीनम् ॥ १७-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Lord's Boon:
Pleased with the devotion and prayers of Dhruva, the Lord awarded the abode of Dhruvapadam.
It is surrounded by all solar systems, planets and stars and all luminaries in the sky. No one had ever ruled this planet.
The Lord told Dhruva that in future he will rule his father's kingdom for thirty six thousand years & he will not become old.
After enjoying the material life, he will go to the planet of the Lord and never again come back to the material world.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tāvadvibodhavimalaṃ praṇuvantamena-
-mābhāṣathāstvamavagamya tadīyabhāvam |
rājyaṃ ciraṃ samanubhūya bhajasva bhūyaḥ
sarvottaraṃ dhruvapadaṃ vinivṛttihīnam || 17-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
इत्यूचिषि त्वयि गते नृपनन्दनोऽसा-
-वानन्दिताखिलजनो नगरीमुपेतः ।
रेमे चिरं भवदनुग्रहपूर्णकाम-
-स्ताते गते च वनमादृतराज्यभारः ॥ १७-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Dhruva returned to the Kingdom and ruled it peacefully with prosperity, after his father retired to the forest.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ityūciṣi tvayi gate nṛpanandano’sā-
-vānanditākhilajano nagarīmupetaḥ |
reme ciraṃ bhavadanugrahapūrṇakāma-
-stāte gate ca vanamādṛtarājyabhāraḥ || 17-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
यक्षेण देव निहते पुनरुत्तमेऽस्मिन्
यक्षैः स युद्धनिरतो विरतो मनूक्त्या ।
शान्त्या प्रसन्नहृदयाद्धनदादुपेता-
-त्त्वद्भक्तिमेव सुदृढामवृणोन्महात्मा ॥ १७-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Later, Uttama was killed by Yaksha and feeling enraged Dhruva raised a war against Yakshas, but with Swayambhu Manu's advice, he dropped the war. Yaksha king Kubera, pleased with his action, wanted to grant a boon, still Dhruva only wanted the boon of permanent devotion to Lord.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
yakṣeṇa deva nihate punaruttame’smin
yakṣaiḥ sa yuddhanirato virato manūktyā |
śāntyā prasannahṛdayāddhanadādupetā-
-ttvadbhaktimeva sudṛḍhāmavṛṇonmahātmā || 17-10 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अन्ते भवत्पुरुषनीतविमानयातो
मात्रा समं ध्रुवपदे मुदितोऽयमास्ते ।
एवं स्वभृत्यजनपालनलोलधीस्त्वं
वातालयाधिप निरुन्धि ममामयौघान् ॥ १७-११ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: At the most appropriate time, Dhruva along with his mother, was taken to Dhruvalokha by lord's attendants and is living there, ever, happily by Lord's mercy.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ante bhavatpuruṣanītavimānayāto
mātrā samaṃ dhruvapade mudito’yamāste |
evaṃ svabhṛtyajanapālanaloladhīstvaṃ
vātālayādhipa nirundhi mamāmayaughān || 17-11 ||
